Both error paths work. Open **http://maker:4001** and try these two:

**1 — Something that isn't a link.** In the save box type `hello world` and press **Save**. Instead of saving junk, you get an inline note: *"That doesn't look like a link. Paste a web address like https://example.com."* — and nothing is added. It clears as soon as you start typing a real link.

**2 — A page whose details can't be read.** Paste `https://obscure-blog.example/some-post` and press **Save**. The preview still opens (so saving is never blocked), but with a heads-up: *"We couldn't read this page's details automatically…"* It guesses a title from the address, and you can fill in the title, description, tags or a note yourself, then Save.

Two decisions to check:
- I only block saving when the text **isn't a web address at all**. A real link whose page simply can't be read is **still saveable** — you just fill in the details — because I didn't want a flaky page to stop you keeping a link.
- The auto-fill failure is shown as a **non-blocking notice**, not an error.

**Do these two behaviours match what you'd want — block only genuine non-links, but always let a real link be saved even when its details can't be fetched?**
